title: Big, Easy-to-Read Text on an E-Reader: Kobo Clara BW vs. Clara Colour
subtitle: How a small e-reader lets you make text bigger, what the two Kobo Clara models offer, and where they fall short.
excerpt: If small print has made reading a chore, an e-reader lets you change the text size in its menus. Here is how the Kobo Clara BW and Clara Colour compare, and what they cannot do.
author: Nickel And Gadget Editors

sections.content: Many longtime readers reach a point where paperback print feels too small and the lamp never seems bright enough. A heavy hardcover can make the wrists ache, too.

An e-reader is a small, single-purpose device for reading books. Its main benefit for tired eyes is simple: you choose how big the words are. That one setting can bring a lot of reading back within easy reach.

Both Kobo Clara models use a screen technology called E Ink, which is meant to look more like printed paper than a glowing phone or tablet. Kobo describes the Clara BW screen as glare-free. The Clara Colour page describes a color E Ink display, but does not make that glare claim.
The Clara BW has a built-in light called ComfortLight PRO, so you can read in a dim room. The Clara Colour page does not mention a light, so check that on the product before you buy.

Text size is set in the reading menus. Make the letters bigger and each page holds fewer words, so you turn pages more often. On a 6-inch screen like these two, very large text can mean only a few lines per page. The product pages do not state the largest text size either model offers, so confirm it on the device itself before you rely on it.

Both models come from Rakuten Kobo. The Clara BW has a black-and-white screen. The Clara Colour has a color display and shows full-color book covers. For plain novels and nonfiction, black-and-white may be all you need.
One thing to decide before buying: which bookstore you want. As NBC Select put it in its 2026 e-reader roundup:
"Typically, e-reader manufacturers only let you purchase ebooks through their brand's compatible storefronts." — NBC Select
In plain terms, books bought from Kobo do not move over to a Kindle, and Kindle books do not move to a Kobo. If someone already has a shelf of Kindle books, a Kobo will not open them.

items: Bookstore first: pick the device that matches the store the reader already uses or plans to use.
Text size in person: if a display model is available to try, look at the largest text setting to see whether it is big enough. Otherwise, ask about the return policy.
Screen size: a 6-inch screen is small to hold, but shows fewer words at large sizes. Someone with severe low vision may do better with a bigger screen or a magnifier.
Extra costs: cases, sleep covers and a stylus are sold separately. Reading subscriptions such as Kobo Plus are optional and carry their own fee, so check current pricing.
Audiobooks: these models have no built-in speaker. Listening requires Bluetooth headphones or a Bluetooth speaker.
Returns and warranty: the Clara BW page lists a 45-day return and an included warranty. The Clara Colour page does not list return terms, so check them before buying, especially as a gift.

sections.content: Setting it up for comfortable reading
Once the device is set up, open a book and make the text bigger right away, so the first experience is a comfortable one rather than squinting at the default size.
Adjust the light to suit the room if your model has one. The Clara BW also offers an optional Dark Mode, so it is worth trying it on and off to see which you prefer.

An e-reader makes text bigger, but it does not treat or correct eyesight. If reading has suddenly become harder, or print looks blurry or distorted, check in with an eye doctor. For very low vision, a handheld video magnifier may be a better match, and we cover those in our magnifier guides.
sections.label: Good to Know

sections.content: What an e-reader will not do

These are reading devices only. They do not play video, run the kinds of apps a tablet does, or play sound without headphones or a Bluetooth speaker. If the person you are shopping for wants video calls, games or a built-in speaker, a tablet is the better choice.
Prices on e-readers move around, and Kobo runs holiday promotions, so it pays to check the price on the day you buy.
Start with the bookstore question, check the text size on the device, and then enjoy the next chapter.
